title: Agent-Based Econophysics as an Equilibrium Computation Method
research_question: Can many-agent simulations of policy-optimal decisions replicate the stationary and transition distributions of the same heterogeneous-agent general equilibrium model?
feasibility_hypothesis: Yes as a numerical representation, provided the simulated decision rules solve the same equilibrium and common/aggregate risk is consistently forecast.
mechanisms: Individual agents use verified Bellman policies
Finite-N Markov evolution and seed-controlled Monte Carlo
state_variables: individual asset and income state arrays
required_equations: Discrete Kolmogorov or histogram distribution evolution
Law of motion of aggregate states
comparison_baseline: Distributional operator solution of Stage 0 at the same prices and shocks
acceptance_tests: Particle distribution converges to stationary measure as N and time increase
Policies agree with Stage 0 over the state grid
Aggregate resource and financial asset accounting
Multiple-seed confidence intervals and reproducible run manifests
stage_gate: Treat ABM as an implementation method, not as a free-standing economic microfoundation.

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
